guide.summary: Each customer authorizes the app separately through the OAuth 2.0 flow and selects the pages to share. The permission boundary is Read content only, with no insert or update capabilities, and workspaces outside one selected set require a public integration.

findings.title: Per-user OAuth 2.0 authorization with user-tied access token
findings.detail: OAuth integrations let each user authorize the app separately; the app then uses an access token tied to that user for API requests. Each connecting customer must complete the flow individually.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers connect their own Notion accounts to read pages they share.

evidence.quote: a user-scoped static token, and OAuth integrations and public integrations use the OAuth 2.0 protocol.
Use an OAuth integration when your internal tool needs to act on behalf of each person who uses it. Each user authorizes the app separately and grants it access to
content. Your app uses an access token tied to that user.

findings.title: Read content capability for reading shared pages and blocks
findings.detail: Read content allows retrieving pages, page markdown and block children, but not updating databases or pages. It does not grant insert or update capability, so the app stays read-only.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to the confirmed read-only use case; no other content capability is needed.

evidence.quote: Read content : This capability gives a connection access to read existing content in a Notion workspace. For example, a connection with only this capability is able to call Retrieve
a database , but not Update database .
​ Errors The connection needs read content capabilities . Missing capabilities return 403 . A missing page or missing access returns 404 .

findings.title: Customers must share pages through the page picker
findings.detail: During authorization the user selects pages to share; the picker only shows pages the user has full access to. Pages not shared with the connection return 404 errors.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to every customer who authorizes; only shared pages and their children are readable.

findings.detail: Scoped integrations can only be installed in the workspaces chosen at creation and cannot be listed on the Marketplace. Making the app available to any workspace requires a public integration, and installation scope cannot be changed later.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies because other customer organizations and workspaces will connect.

steps.title: Create a public OAuth integration with redirect URI and read-only capability

blockers.title: Read titles and content of pages customers explicitly share with the integration
blockers.resolution: The title path assumes a literal properties.title key, but for data-source pages the title property key is user-configured, so the step should locate the property with type title (documented example properties.Title.title[]) and join its title[].plain_text; the content step also omits the documented block-children fallback for unsupported block types (bookmarks, embeds, link previews) that markdown returns as unknown, so it should add a recursive block-children read for those blocks. Affected steps: read-shared-page-retrieve, read-shared-page-content.
